title: Sednit_Xagent_Investigation_2bd
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Sednit Xagent backdoor infection on a compromised network. The Sednit group is known for using Xagent for espionage activities, including executing commands from a remote server, collecting sensitive information, and maintaining persistence on infected systems. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Sednit Xagent backdoor infection on a compromised network. The Sednit group is known for using Xagent for espionage activities, including executing commands from a remote server, collecting sensitive information, and maintaining persistence on infected systems. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual activity on the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unauthorized. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified a suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. Investigate the persistence mechanisms used by the service.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can examine the systemd service files and timers. Use the `systemctl list-unit-files` command to list all unit files and look for any related to the suspicious service. The hidden flag is the name of the persistence mechanism or identifier.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To identify the network port used for C2 communication, you can use the `ss -tulnp` command to list all listening ports. Look for any ports that seem suspicious or are not part of the standard services. The hidden flag is the C2 port number.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports.
